subject: two-block pls (or plsDA?) using shape vs categorical variables

messages.author: 1cb68adbec0995e8
messages.subject: two-block pls (or plsDA?) using shape vs categorical variables
parts:
Hi again all,

     I recently stumbled on an analysis plsDA (partial least squares-discriminant analysis) that could potentially be more appropriate for my study and I wondered what you all thought. I am trying to explore the patterns of covariation between the shape of my 92 fish species (shape of each individual measured has been averaged within species) and my suite of multi-leveled categorical environmental factors. So, this is obviously a very preliminary and exploratory study in nature. From the little I have read so far it seems like most people do not use or advise using plsDA, but there was a note that it may be an appropriate method for exploratory studies. What I really want to be able to show is the strength of relationship between my two blocks and transformation grids of what particular shape is associated with each combination of the levels of all my factors because I'm interested in the directionality of the relationship between shape and environment, not JUST whether there is one. Does that make sense? 

   If this seems feasible I would love to hear what you all think and suggest and/or if you have any citations I can check out to make this all happen I'd really appreciate it. Thanks for all you do to help!

Jessica
